title: Aśoka and the Decline of the Mauryas
author: Romila Thapar
note: The classic study of Ashoka's reign and the edicts; the source of the long-running debate on what dhamma meant.

title: The Mauryas Revisited
author: Romila Thapar
note: Thapar's later lectures, which revise her own earlier picture of a highly centralised state.

title: Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300
author: Romila Thapar
note: A readable survey; the Mauryan chapters are a good next step after this page.

title: A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India: From the Stone Age to the 12th Century
author: Upinder Singh
note: A textbook that sets out the evidence (inscriptions, coins, archaeology, texts) alongside the narrative.

title: Ashoka in Ancient India
author: Nayanjot Lahiri
note: A biography of Ashoka built closely on the inscriptions and the places where they were set up.

title: King, Governance, and Law in Ancient India: Kauṭilya's Arthaśāstra
author: Patrick Olivelle (translator)
note: A modern English translation of the Arthashastra, with an introduction on when and how the text was composed.

title: Inscriptions of Asoka (Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. I, new edition)
author: E. Hultzsch
publisher: Clarendon Press, for the Government of India
note: The standard older edition of the edicts, with texts and English translations. Out of copyright in many countries; check before reusing.

title: Ancient India as Described by Megasthenes and Arrian
author: J. W. McCrindle (translator)
note: English translation of the surviving fragments of Megasthenes' Indica, as quoted by later Greek and Roman writers.
